clue.text: A funny lady to appear in need, somehow

parts.note: to come is to appear or show up

indicators.note: somehow says the letters of the following words are arranged in some other way

explanation.surface: A woman with a sense of humour turns up when someone is in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'need' reads as hardship in the surface, but it is part of the material that 'somehow' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A comedienne is a female comic, a woman whose job is making people laugh.

clue.text: The players' shed

explanation.surface: A shed belonging to the members of a sports team.
explanation.definitionFit: The players in a play form its cast, and to cast skin or leaves is to shed them.

clue.text: Candida's husband gets over love for Cherry

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece gets placed over, above, the next

parts.note: in Shaw's play Candida the heroine is married to the Reverend James Morell
love is nil in tennis scoring, written as the round letter O

explanation.surface: A husband gets over his love for a woman called Cherry.
explanation.walkthrough: Shaw's play Candida (1894) centres on the clergyman James Morell and his wife; 'gets over' sets MORELL above O in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The morello is a dark sour variety of cherry used in cooking and jams.

clue.text: Disc jockey's abbreviated attire

parts.note: the abbreviation for a radio presenter, two letters, is also the short form of a formal evening garment

explanation.surface: What a radio presenter wears when dressed down.
explanation.walkthrough: DJ stands both for disc jockey and for the formal evening jacket; 'abbreviated' looks like skimpy clothing but means the letters DJ.
explanation.definitionFit: The garment shortened to DJ is a man's black-tie evening jacket worn for formal dinners.

clue.text: On change of scene the lady has to vanish

parts.note: Eva is a woman's name, standing for any lady

indicators.note: a change of the word scene means its letters are altered in order

explanation.surface: When the setting changes, the actress must disappear from the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' and 'has' are only links; 'change of' signals the rearrangement, and 'the lady' stands for a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: To evanesce is to fade away or disappear like vapour.

clue.text: Water course, say, for invalid with a heavy head

parts.note: null, as in null and void, means invalid

indicators.note: the head of the word heavy is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A stream is suggested as treatment for a sick person with a bad headache.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invalid' reads as a sick person but means NULL; 'head' takes H from 'heavy'.
explanation.definitionFit: A nullah is an Indian ravine or stream bed, a channel for water.

clue.text: Eat away with others and start to hiccup

parts.note: etc, short for et cetera, means and others

indicators.note: the start to a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Eating with company and then beginning to hiccup.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to corrode a surface with acid, wearing it away.

clue.text: African bird has to travel with ring round bill

indicators.note: the ring is placed round, at the foot of, the bill in this down entry

parts.note: to tour is to travel around
AC is the abbreviation for account, a bill
a ring is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: An African bird must fly with a ring around its beak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bill' looks like a beak but is AC, account; 'round' sets the ring O after it.
explanation.definitionFit: The touraco, or turaco, is a brightly coloured fruit-eating bird of African forests.

clue.text: Old soldier is tipsy — hide barrel!

indicators.note: tipsy means drunk and unsteady, so the following letters reel into a new order

explanation.surface: A veteran is drunk, so hide the beer barrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A halberdier was a soldier armed with a halberd, a medieval axe-headed pike.

clue.text: Psychiatrist, qualified but may accept a reduction

parts.note: shrink is slang for a psychiatrist
able means competent or qualified

explanation.surface: A psychiatrist is qualified but might take a pay cut.
explanation.definitionFit: Something shrinkable can be made smaller, so it is capable of being reduced in size.

clue.text: The place to find a 20

parts.note: the cross-reference is to a shellfish that clings to the underside of ships

explanation.surface: Where a certain item is to be found.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 across is BARNACLE; barnacles cling to the part of a ship below the waterline.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's body below deck is where barnacles attach themselves.

clue.text: Get rich on the gravy train

definitions.text: Get rich on the gravy train

parts.words: Get rich on the gravy train
parts.note: read literally, the railway's wagons and carriages are what rolls along on any train, gravy or not

explanation.surface: Make money easily from a cushy position.
explanation.walkthrough: Rich people are said to be rolling in it and to have stock; the gravy train is just a railway train.
explanation.definitionFit: Rolling stock is the locomotives and carriages that run on a railway.

clue.text: Chimney pipe causing vocal complaint

indicators.note: vocal means spoken out loud, so the illness's name is heard rather than seen

parts.note: a complaint is an illness, here influenza

explanation.surface: A smoky chimney gives someone a sore throat.
explanation.definitionFit: A flue is a duct carrying smoke and gases up through a chimney.

clue.text: To prepare the way back, speak to 4

indicators.note: back means the preceding word is read from right to left

parts.note: to pave the way is to prepare it
to orate is to speak formally

explanation.surface: Instructions to clear a path and then make a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns PAVE into EVAP; 4 down is EVANESCE, vanish.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean fade away into nothing, like vapour disappearing.

clue.text: Sailors round on mad rabble — may be drunk

parts.note: an AB is an able seaman, so ABS are sailors
round is the round letter O

indicators.note: mad means wild, so the letters of rabble are scrambled

explanation.surface: Sailors turn on an angry mob, perhaps after drinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' rearranges RABBLE into RBABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something absorbable can be soaked up, taken in as a liquid is.

clue.text: Device for removing inverted military footgear

indicators.note: inverted means turned the other way, so the two halves change places

parts.note: a jackboot is a tall military boot

explanation.surface: A device for taking off upside-down army boots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inverted' swaps the halves of JACKBOOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A bootjack is a forked device you put your heel into to pull off a boot.

clue.text: A not wholly typical Mondrian tree

indicators.note: not wholly means only part of the following words is used, a run inside them

explanation.surface: A typical Mondrian painting of a tree, only partly done.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit inside 'typicAL MONDrian'; Mondrian was a Dutch abstract painter.
explanation.definitionFit: The almond is a tree of the rose family grown for its edible nut.

clue.text: The obvious place to find excellent climbing shrub?

parts.note: a garden is the natural place for a shrub

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means the word is read upwards

parts.note: A1 means excellent, written as letters AI

explanation.surface: Where you would expect to find a first-rate climbing plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' looks like the plant's habit but turns AI upwards to IA.
explanation.definitionFit: Gardenia is an evergreen bush with fragrant white flowers.

clue.text: Room of fellow in charge needs key

parts.note: E is a musical key

explanation.surface: A fellow in charge of a room must have a key to it.
explanation.definitionFit: An office is a room where business or clerical work is done.

clue.text: Hotchpotch from Wells, perhaps, about an artist

indicators.note: about means going around, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: Wells partners Fargo in the name of the American express company Wells Fargo
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A muddle in a book by H G Wells concerning a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wells' suggests the novelist but completes Wells Fargo; FARGO goes about RA.
explanation.definitionFit: A farrago is a confused mixture, a jumble.

clue.text: The result of a wild goose chase for a placeman?

definitions.text: The result of a wild goose chase for a placeman?

parts.words: The result of a wild goose chase for a placeman
parts.note: hunting a certain wild goose bags it, and an office-holder who clings to his post is named after the same clinging shellfish

explanation.surface: What a political hanger-on gets from a pointless search.
explanation.walkthrough: The barnacle goose is a wild goose; a barnacle is also a hanger-on who clings to an office.
explanation.definitionFit: A clinging placeman, someone who stays stuck to a sinecure, is likened to the shellfish fixed to a hull.

clue.text: Opposed to church that's non-militant

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
i.e., id est, means that is

explanation.surface: Being against the church is a peaceful stance.
explanation.walkthrough: CONCHIE is British slang for a conscientious objector, one who refuses military service.
explanation.definitionFit: A conscientious objector is a pacifist who will not fight.

clue.text: A picture on the wall put up as a warning

indicators.note: put up in a down clue means the word is set upwards, read backwards

parts.note: a mural is a picture painted on a wall

explanation.surface: A picture hung on the wall as a caution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' looks like hanging the picture but turns MURAL into LARUM.
explanation.definitionFit: An alarum is an old word for an alarm, a call to arms.

clue.text: Like a Martini-Henry — doubly so!

parts.note: the Victorian army rifle has a tube for the bullet, and a shotgun has two of them

explanation.surface: Comparing something to an old army rifle, twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: The Martini-Henry was a 19th-century British service rifle; double-barrelled is the twice-over sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A gun with a barrel is described as barrelled, and a shotgun with two is double-barrelled.

clue.text: Five French said to have drowned here

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the French number is heard as an English word

parts.note: cinq is French for five

explanation.surface: Five French people are reported to have drowned at this spot.
explanation.definitionFit: To sink is to go under water, as a drowning person does.

clue.text: Congeal into a cold mass

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
a lot is a large quantity, a mass

explanation.surface: Something setting into a solid frozen lump.
explanation.definitionFit: To clot is to thicken and solidify, as blood does.

clue.text: Dickens admits a widow. Ruth, married him

indicators.note: admits means lets in, so one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: Boz was the pen name of Charles Dickens

explanation.surface: Dickens writes about a widow; Ruth married him.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Bible the widow Ruth marries Boaz.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Book of Ruth the widowed Moabite marries her kinsman, the landowner of Bethlehem.

clue.text: Dictator chap, an admirer of Marianne

parts.note: Franco was the dictator of Spain
Phil is a man's name, any chap

explanation.surface: A dictator who is a fan of a woman named Marianne.
explanation.walkthrough: Marianne is the national symbol of France.
explanation.definitionFit: Marianne personifies France, so someone who admires her is a lover of France.

clue.text: Tearful lady went back without one to the poetic wood

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is removed
went back means the name is read in reverse

parts.note: in Greek myth Niobe wept endlessly for her slain children
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A weeping woman retreated alone into the wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'went back' turns NIOBE into EBOIN, and 'without' then drops the I.
explanation.definitionFit: Ebon is the literary word for ebony, the black hardwood.

clue.text: The obvious place on the Thames for a levee?

definitions.text: The obvious place on the Thames for a levee?

parts.words: The obvious place on the Thames for a levee
parts.note: a levee is a raised flood bank, and London's riverside road takes its name from one

explanation.surface: Where on the river to hold a royal reception.
explanation.walkthrough: A levee is also a royal reception, the misleading sense; the Thames has a famous raised bank in London.
explanation.definitionFit: A levee is a raised bank holding back a river, the same as a flood wall along the water.
